title: Classic Fantasy Fiction You Know
use_cases: Use when identifying core tropes within the high-fantasy subgenre
Implement when comparing separate-world magic systems vs. hidden-world layers
Configure when establishing world-building rules for low-magic environments
Use when studying character transitions from non-magical to magical planes
content:
- The Lord of the Rings by J.R.R. Tolkien: This is the classic example of Tolkien-style world creation. It is set in Middle-earth. It has elves, dwarves, wizards, and a Dark Lord. Magic is powerful and a key part of the plot.
- Harry Potter by J.K. Rowling: This is a perfect example. It is set in “our” world, but the magical world is completely separate. There is a hidden world (Diagon Alley, Hogwarts). Magic is a skill you learn in school. Non-magic people (muggles) do not know about it and would be shocked.
- A Game of Thrones by George R.R. Martin: This is “low fantasy” at first, meaning magic is rare. But it is still fantasy. It is set in a new world (Westeros). It has dragons, old magic, and ice zombies. The characters react to these things as powerful and world-changing.
- The Chronicles of Narnia by C.S. Lewis: Characters from our world travel to a different, magical world. This is a clear sign of fantasy.
